title: Flamenco
objective: After this level you can describe flamenco's guitar, song and dance.
summary: Flamenco, from Andalusia with an essential Gitano (Roma) role, fuses song (cante), dance (baile) and guitar (toque), held together by the compas, a 12-beat cycle mixing groups of three and two.

cards.headline: Flamenco is three arts at once: song, dance and guitar.
cards.body: In 2010, UNESCO added flamenco to its list of humanity's intangible cultural heritage. Its heartland is Andalusia in southern Spain, and the Gitano (Roma) community has played an essential role in its development. UNESCO describes it as a fusion of song (cante), dance (baile) and musicianship (toque). Take them one at a time, then find the clock that holds them together.

cards.headline: Cante: the heart of it
cards.body: Britannica calls cante, song, the essence of flamenco, and its most profound style is cante jondo, 'deep song.' The singer, a man or a woman, preferably sits, with no backing singers. The lyrics are brief and simple, and they can carry grief, joy, tragedy or fear. In flamenco's golden age, roughly 1780 to 1845, song came first.

cards.headline: Guitar, dance and hands
cards.body: The guitar began as accompaniment, and UNESCO says toque has long outgrown that role. Dance moved to the center in the mid-19th century, after cafes cantantes, commercial venues opening from 1842, put musicians and dancers on show. Dancers use arms, torso, hands and fingers, along with footwork and heelwork. Around them come handclaps, foot-stamping and sometimes castanets, so the rhythm section is often the people themselves.

cards.headline: Compas: count to twelve
cards.body: What keeps singer, guitarist and dancers together is the compas: a 12-beat cycle with groups of three and two arranged inside it, accented in traditional ways. Soleares, a fundamental form of deep song, moves at a slow twelve-beat pace. Remember Level 4: listeners tend to hear beats in groups of two or three. Flamenco uses both inside a single cycle, and every performer counts the same twelve.

mascot.line: Clapping along? Count to twelve, not four. The compas is the clock.

cards.headline: Flamenco: felt
learned: Cante, baile and toque: song, dance, guitar
Andalusia is its heartland; Gitanos shaped it
Cante is its essence; cante jondo is deep song
The compas: 12 beats in groups of three and two

questions.prompt: UNESCO describes flamenco as a fusion of which three arts?

options.label: Painting, poetry and street theater
options.rationale: Flamenco is performed music and movement.

options.label: Opera, ballet and orchestral music from Madrid
Drums, brass horns and a large choir of backing singers
options.rationale: Flamenco uses a solo singer, guitar and handclaps.

options.label: Song, dance and musicianship (cante, baile, toque)

questions.explanation: Flamenco fuses cante (song), baile (dance) and toque (musicianship, above all guitar).

questions.prompt: What job does the compas do in a flamenco performance?

options.label: It sets which key the guitarist must play in
options.rationale: The compas is rhythmic, not a key.

options.label: Its 12-beat cycle keeps singer, guitarist and dancers together
It tells the singer which verses and lyrics to choose
options.rationale: Lyrics aren't set by the rhythm cycle.

options.label: It replaces the guitar in slow songs like soleares
options.rationale: The compas is a count, not an instrument.

questions.explanation: The compas is the shared 12-beat cycle that coordinates everyone performing.

questions.prompt: Level 4 said listeners hear beats in groups of two or three. How does flamenco's compas use those groups?

options.label: It uses only groups of two, like a march
options.rationale: The compas mixes threes in too.

options.label: It uses only groups of three, like a waltz
options.rationale: The compas mixes twos in too.

options.label: It arranges groups of three and two inside one 12-beat cycle
It avoids grouping its twelve beats at all
options.rationale: Grouping and accent are its whole design.

questions.explanation: The compas arranges groups of three and two inside a 12-beat cycle, accented in traditional patterns.
